newsitem.title: USA: Search resumes for clues to Michigan plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Search resumes for clues to Michigan plane crash.

text.p: Crash investigators for a second day on Saturday combed through wreckage of a commuter plane that nosedived into a snow-covered Michigan field, killing all 29 people on board.

Aviation officials in Washington began analysing the flight data and cockpit voice recorders recovered on Friday from a blackened crater left by the crash of the Delta Comair plane Thursday afternoon.
The disaster killed 28 adults and one infant.

National Transportation Safety Board Member John Hammerschmidt, the lead investigator, said the boxes were slightly damaged, but otherwise are expected to yield important information about why the plane, a Brasilia built by Embraer of Brazil, went down.
Speculation on the cause has centred on the snow and icy weather conditions the plane was flying in as it prepared to land at Detroit's Metropolitan Airport.
Some observers have also suggested the crash could have been caused by broken propeller blades. Propeller problems have been blamed for two previous fatal crashes involving the Brasilia model.

Flight 3272 was enroute to Detroit from Cincinnati when it went down about 25 miles (40 kms) south of the airport in rural Monroe County in southeast Michigan. Witnesses said the plane did several barrel rolls before it slammed into the ground at a sharp angle.
Strong winds that pushed windchill factors well below zero and created temporary whiteout conditions have hampered the recovery of human remains.
